title: Classes
summary: Fields, constructors, methods, static members and inheritance.

increment(): this {              // methods use `this.` explicitly, always
static fromString(s: string) {   // static member: Counter.fromString("5")
Differences from C#: there is no implicit `this` (writing `count += 1` is an error), members are public by default, and there is only one constructor.
> **Tip:** TypeScript's shortcut `constructor(private name: string)` (parameter properties) is not plain JavaScript, so Node's type stripping rejects it. Declare the field and assign it, as above.

steps.explain: A class is a special kind of function under the hood, so `typeof Temp` is `"function"`.

steps.prompt: Inside a method of `Counter`, why does `count += 1;` fail when `this.count += 1;` works?
options: JavaScript has no implicit `this`: a bare `count` looks for a variable, not a field
steps.explain: In C# `count` would resolve to the field. In JavaScript you always write `this.` to reach a member.

steps.title: Inheritance
body: override speak() {                  // `override` is optional TS, but catches typos
Every method is effectively `virtual`: there is no `virtual`/`sealed`. `instanceof` checks the prototype chain: `new Dog("Rex") instanceof Animal` is `true`.
Keep hierarchies shallow. Modern TypeScript code uses far fewer classes than C#; plain objects, functions and composition (lesson 3) do most of the work.

steps.title: Shapes
prompt: Write a base class `Shape` with a `name: string` field set by the constructor, a method `area(): number` that returns `0`, and a method `describe(): string` returning `"<name> with area <area to 2 decimals>"`.
Then write `Circle extends Shape` (constructor takes `radius`, name `"circle"`) and `Rect extends Shape` (takes `w` and `h`, name `"rect"`), each overriding `area`.
template: Dojo.eq("new Circle(1).describe()", "circle with area 3.14", new Circle(1).describe());
Dojo.eq("new Rect(2, 3.5).describe()", "rect with area 7.00", new Rect(2, 3.5).describe());
Dojo.eq("sum of areas", 9, Math.round([new Rect(2, 3), new Circle(1)].reduce((s, x) => s + x.area(), 0)));
Dojo.check("Circle is a Shape", new Circle(2) instanceof Shape, "Circle should extend Shape");
hints: `describe` in the base calls `this.area()`, which runs the subclass's version.
